To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the immobile elements, Zr and Ti, are useful for stratigraphic correlation and for the determination of primary pre-alteration, pre metamorphism composition of metavolc anic rocks, (2) the relative concentration of the immobile Zr and Ti can be used to distinguish altered rocks of different origin and (3) the Zr and Ti ratios are very useful in the detection and quantification of hydrothermal alteration/mineralization.

the Zr/Ti ratios are useful in the following: (1) (1) Recognition of primary premetamorphic volcanic rock types (2) (2) Determination of the original composition and stratigraphic position of variably altered metavolcanics (3) (3) Recognition of the original composition, stratigraphic position and alteration/mineralization history of massive sulphide deposits.

the use of the immobile element Zr/Ti in lithogeochemistry is a powerful and reliable tool for the exploration of massive sulphide deposits, especially in complex Precambrian terrains, where the recognition of alteration zones, stratigraphic correlation and the recognition and delineation of mineralized zones are of paramount importance.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a rock geochemical method for the exploration of massive sulphide deposits which is independent of the type of alteration, metamorphism and deformation which may have affected the host rocks, and independent of the stratigraphic position and the size of the ore deposit.
the use of Zr and Ti as immobile elements in the exploration for massive sulphides in the Pecos belt of New Mexico.
the application of immobile element ratios in the recognition and interpretation of alteration trends in the Jones Hill massive sulphide deposit, Pecos greenbelt, New Mexico.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Jones Hill deposit was formed by the emplacement of a large body of massive sulphides (and associated gangue minerals) into a pre existing stratigraphy.

rock geochemical data, particularly when supported by mineralogical, petrographic and alteration data, provide an excellent tool for the delineation of alteration and mineralization anomalies in a structurally complex and highly altered terrain such as the Mid Proterozoc Pecos greenston belt.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of the immobile element ratios Zr/Ti and Zr/Zr+Ti (or Zr/Ti vs Zr/Zr + Ti) is an effective tool in the exploration and evaluation of massive sulphide deposits, especially in areas of complex geological structures and alteration/mineralization histories.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rock geochemical exploration for massive sulfides can be successful in greenstone belts, even in areas where the rocks have undergone extensive alteration.
the immobile elements Ti and Zr are excellent indicators of primary volcanic source rocks, and of the alteration/mineralization process.
the Zr/Ti ratios can be used as a guide in the exploration for massive sulphides and other mineral deposits.
